title: STOP.
paragraphs:
STOP.
This isn’t just another post.
You almost scrolled past this… didn’t you?

A weight.
A whisper.
A quiet “this is about you.”
You’ve mastered the art of hiding.

Smiling in public.
Serving in church.
Posting faith… while fighting secret battles no one sees.
Because the louder your image gets…

You said,
“I’ll deal with it later.”
It doesn’t even feel like conviction anymore.
But when it stops shocking you.
But deep down, there’s this quiet question:
“Why do I feel so far from God?”
“Wake up, O sleeper, rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.” — Ephesians 5:14
Paul is speaking to people who thought they were fine…

Some scholars interpret this as an early Christian hymn—
a call to believers who had grown comfortable in compromise.
But because you don’t realize what’s happening around you.
“Whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy.” — Proverbs 28:13

Not hides.
Not manages.
Not justifies.
You can’t heal what you keep hiding.
You can’t be free from what you protect.
Because if you bring it into the light…
Because the Gospel doesn’t expose you to destroy you.
It exposes you to redeem you.
Jesus already saw the worst version of you.
The one behind the filters, the roles, the excuses.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not after you cleaned up your life.
While you were still in it.
That guilt that keeps whispering, “you’re too far gone”?
He silenced it with His blood.
You are more sinful than you want to admit…
But more loved than you ever imagined.
Grace is not permission to stay the same.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
And here’s the question that will follow you after you close this:
Will you answer… or will you silence it again?
If this stirred something deep in you…
